Below budget
— — Grey tracts hold under 100 households and are excluded, per the data dictionary.

Every tract clears a different bar, made of different things.

Colour shows how many households fall short, tract by tract — same reading as any choropleth. Click a tract and the panel answers the next question: in this specific place, what does that gap actually consist of — rent, childcare, transportation, something else?

Click any of the county's 727 reliable tracts. The panel shows the same mean-monthly balance sheet the county figure is built from — housing, transportation, healthcare, food, other essentials, childcare, broadband, and tax — computed for that tract's own households below budget, not estimated from the county average.

Method & limits

What "gap" means here

Same balance sheet as the calculator's own "why they fall short" section, just sliced by tract instead of county-wide: mean monthly amounts, among a tract's own households below their budget, for the same seven cost components (plus tax) that sum to hlb_year. Means, not medians, so the column adds up on screen.

Tracts, not places

Geography here is the 2020 census tract (geoid), the same 727 tracts used everywhere else in this project (five of 732 dropped for holding under 100 households). There is no ZIP code in this dataset, and a tract-to-ZIP crosswalk would not preserve the thresholds shown — so this page does not offer one.

Small-tract uncertainty

Rows are cloned from 55,218 PUMS donors; a tract's own mean is a statistic over however many synthetic households sit in it below budget, not a census of it. Tracts flagged in the panel report a smaller count and should be read with that in mind — the donor-adjusted confidence interval on any tract-level rate in this project is ±3.1pp.

Two tracts held out of the featured set

06073009510 and 06073009511 carry the signature of military family housing — BAH excluded from recorded income while this model still charges full market rent. They are shown on the map and clickable like any other tract, flagged rather than corrected, per Method & limits.

Same caveats as everywhere else

Rows are synthetic households, valid for distributions and geography, never for claims about individuals. No time dimension: this is a 2024 snapshot, not a trend.
